subject: reasoning
question: In the following question, in each option a pair of figures is given. In each pair the figure towards the left of (:) is related by some logic/rule/relation with the figure on the right of (:). Select the odd figure pair from the given alternatives.
solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: In both sets of figures, the odd pair is identified by **breaking the established pattern**.

Now, the checking Options:

Option 1: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/26911e3652b2086659a666f8635d8b410d3c1bd117804fb36192a05074434f60.png] 

4 sides, 4 lines → Follows rule

Option 2: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d0b892dcf75ca5a7a28421e91ee3fa9401cc87a9159441a23079874f25eb0dea.png] 

5 sides, 5 lines → Follows rule

Option 3: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1f53319ce5bc0c67f52057614076d9a7ae3f56cd0a9f5c5cdc74f19d5580be2.png] 

4 sides, 4 lines → Follows rule

Option 4: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b5b286e8a1150ec428415bfb5259c22256ae6e5a4735f164740517ec74cccbfe.png] 

3 sides, 4 lines → Odd one out

The rule is *number of sides = number of lines crossing the shape*. Option 4 (triangle with 4 lines) breaks this rule.

Hence, the correct answer for both sets is Option 4.
